subject: maths
question: A man walks to a viewpoint and returns to the starting point by his car maintaining constant speed and thus takes a total time of 7 hours 45 minutes. He would have gained 6 hours by driving both ways. How long would it have taken for him to walk both ways with same walking speed?
solution:
**Given:**

Total time when walking one way and returning by car = 7 hours 45 minutes = 7.75 hours

Time gained if driving both ways = 6 hours

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Total time = Sum of individual times

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time taken if driving both ways = 7.75 − 6 = 1.75 hours

⇒ Let distance = D

⇒ Let walking speed = w

⇒ Let car speed = c

⇒ Time taken to drive both ways = 2D ÷ c

⇒ 2D ÷ c = 1.75

⇒ D ÷ c = 0.875

⇒ Time taken to walk one way = Total time − Driving time one way

⇒ D ÷ w = 7.75 − 0.875 = 6.875

⇒ Time taken to walk both ways = 2D ÷ w

⇒ Time taken to walk both ways = 2 × 6.875 = 13.75 hours

⇒ 13.75 hours = 13 hours 45 minutes

**∴ The man would have taken 13 hours 45 minutes to walk both ways.**
